whatItDoes.text: Approves the Development and Funding Agreement, a guaranty and a team non-relocation agreement for a Rays ballpark and mixed-use district on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus, at Dale Mabry Highway and West Tampa Bay Boulevard. WUSF reported that the county's share is capped at $796 million, including $360 million from the Community Investment Tax (a half-cent sales tax), $263 million backed by the tourist development tax, $103 million in other county funds and $30 million in federal disaster-recovery money (those listed amounts total $756 million; WUSF did not explain the difference), while the Rays pay more than $1.3 billion plus all cost overruns. The county said the Rays plan to open the ballpark in April 2029, and that the board still had to approve a ballpark license and use agreement, a community benefits agreement and a construction funds trust agreement.

afterward.text: A majority of the board approved an interlocal agreement making the Tampa Sports Authority the county's representative under the Development and Funding Agreement. The authority will oversee design documents, construction materials, schedules and budgets for the stadium.

rays-final.note: Supporters, including Chair Ken Hagan and Commissioner Cohen, cited the project's size and its effect on the region's profile; Commissioner Wostal objected to using Community Investment Tax money, which he said was marketed to voters in 2024 as not going to a stadium (WUSF). WUSF said bond validation and groundbreaking were expected the following month, but I found no source confirming either happened. The license and use, community benefits and construction trust agreements were not found as approved by Oct 27, 2026. The length of the non-relocation term was not in the sources I read.

whatItDoes.text: At the July 29 budget reconciliation hearing, commissioners voted 7 to 0 to approve changes to items they had flagged in the recommended FY 2027 budget, which the county described as a proposed $14.1 billion budget, including a millage swap to support public safety and other services, per a Govly meeting summary. The summary says the board discussed moving money from some nonprofits back to county departments for local infrastructure, but it does not list the individual changes or the tax rates. The vote applied to the recommended budget; the final FY 2027 budget and tax rates were adopted later.

afterward.text: The county's property tax page, last updated Oct 16, 2026, said the adopted FY 2027 budget cut the countywide property tax rate to 5.3608 mills, down from 5.4608 in FY 2026, and set the unincorporated-area rate at 4.7163 mills. It said about 70% of the adopted unincorporated-area general fund goes to public safety.

whatItDoes.text: Approves a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Tampa Bay Rays and the City of Tampa for a ballpark and mixed-use district on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus. It passed 5 to 2 on May 20, 2026. Because it was non-binding, it set the terms for the final contracts but did not commit county money by itself; the final agreements came up for a separate vote in August. WWSB reported a total project cost of about $2.3 billion and a county share in the MOU of up to $796 million ($360 million Community Investment Tax, more than $260 million in tourist tax bonds and $103 million in other county funds).

afterward.text: The Tampa City Council approved the city's part of the final stadium deal 4 to 3.

The County Commission voted 5 to 2 to approve the Development and Funding Agreement, guaranty and team non-relocation agreement, with the county's share capped at $796 million. WUSF reported that figure was $100 million less than the May MOU.
A majority of the board approved an interlocal agreement with the Tampa Sports Authority to act as the county's representative under the Development and Funding Agreement.

rays-mou.note: The sources disagree on the MOU's county share: WWSB says up to $796 million in May, while WUSF says the final $796 million was $100 million less than the MOU. I did not read the MOU text. WWSB's itemized amounts add up to about $723 million, so part of the $796 million is not broken out.

whatItDoes.text: The board approved this package 4 to 3 on Oct 21, 2026, after a public hearing, with Commissioners Cohen, Hagan and Myers voting no; on Oct 7 it had voted 4 to 3 to move toward finalizing the agreement. Approves a 15-year agreement under which the county pays ZooTampa up to $75 million, $5 million a year through 2041, from Community Investment Tax money (a half-cent sales tax), and the zoo matches it one to one, for about $150 million of work. The plan includes upgrades to older habitats, an expanded elephant habitat, a family coaster and a new South America section that extends across North Boulevard onto about 14 acres now used as a City of Tampa maintenance lot. Some commissioners questioned why other eligible groups such as the Children's Museum, Tampa Bay History Center and Straz Center got nothing from this package, while others noted that the same fund sends far more to the Rays stadium, per Bay News 9.

afterward.text: A majority of the board voted to add ZooTampa capital improvements to the list of projects paid for by the renewed Community Investment Tax. The board also approved an FY 2027 budget amendment putting $5,000,000 in the CIT Extension Project Fund for ZooTampa.

zootampa-75m.note: The vote date is unconfirmed. On Sep 16 a majority told staff to finalize the partnership and set a funding hearing for Oct 7 (county recap). FOX 13 reported a 4 to 3 approval of the funding agreement on Oct 7. Bay News 9 reported a 4 to 3 'final vote' on Oct 21, and the county's Oct 21 recap says the board had 'recently approved' the 15-year agreement. So the agreement was probably approved Oct 7, and the Oct 21 4 to 3 vote may have been the CIT project-list change. How each commissioner voted is not in these sources.
